in-strĕpo , ŭi, ĭtum, 3, v. n.,
I.to make a noise anywhere; to sound, resound, rattle, clatter, creak (mostly poet. and post-class.): sub pondere faginus axis Instrepat, * Verg. G. 3, 172: “dentibus,” to gnash, Claud. Cons. Mall. Theod. 222 .—With a Gr. acc., to make resound, to utter: “lamentabiles questus,” App. M. 2, p. 126, 36 (but in Liv. 4, 43 fin., the correct read. is increparet).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
